data.long_meaning: In Greek, 'evangelist' translates to 'bearer of good news'. This name was given to the early Christian missionaries who traveled and preached the gospel. The term is also used in the New Testament to describe those who spread the teachings of Jesus. The name Evangelist carries the meaning “Bringer of Good News” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Evangelist usually hope their child will grow to embody bringer of good news and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Evangelist
in_english.meaning: one who proclaims the Gospel, announcer of good news
in_english.long_meaning: Evangelist - a term used in Christian tradition to describe a person who proclaims the Gospel of Jesus Christ, often associated with missionary work and the spread of the faith. The term is derived from the Greek Evangelion (εὐαγγέλιον), meaning good news or Gospel. In the New Testament, the term is used to describe the four authors of the Gospels, Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. Modern usage may refer to individuals or groups who proclaim the Gospel, often with a focus on evangelism and mission.

The name “Evangelist” serves as an inspiration and reminder that sharing the Good News is a fundamental aspect of our faith and a way to bring others closer to God.
